findings.description: `"${@:---check}"` turns the explicit "" argument into `--check`, so the "missing title fails" and "missing status fails" tests run in check mode, where the stale index fails them anyway; they cannot detect the validation being removed.
findings.body:
**Concern.** Commit 9bf232d added an explicit `""` argument to the two validation tests (lines 40 and 42) so they run in write mode, where only the new title/status validation can make the script exit 1. But `expect` forwards its arguments as `"${@:---check}"`. In bash, the `:-` form treats `"$@"` holding a single empty argument as null, so the default applies and the script receives `--check`, not `""`.

In check mode, the fixture's README was generated from `0001-first.md` alone. Adding `0002-second.md` always makes the index stale, so `--check` exits 1 whether or not the `[ -z "$title" ] || [ -z "$status" ]` guard in `scripts/adr-index.sh` exists. Both tests stay green with the validation deleted. This is exactly the gap the fix round was meant to close.

```bash
ADR_DIR=$adr bash "$SCRIPT" "${@:---check}" 2>/dev/null
```

The script itself would treat `""` as write mode (`${1:-}` is not `--check`), so the bug is only in the harness's default-argument logic. Fix: default only when no arguments were passed (`$# -eq 0`), and forward `"$@"` as given.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/50460dd2e3276aa15a908e11fb8ced812e8636ec/scripts/adr-index.test.sh#L16-L19
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/50460dd2e3276aa15a908e11fb8ced812e8636ec/scripts/adr-index.test.sh#L39-L42

findings.description: fixture() ends with `ADR_DIR=$dir bash "$SCRIPT" || return 1`, but every call site (`fixture; expect ...`) ignores the return status, and the script has no `set -e`. If the seeding run fails, the test carries on against a half-built fixture. It can then report a misleading FAIL, or a false pass when the expected exit is 1. The function also hands its result back through the global `dir` with no stated contract.

`render` still passes the index with `IDX=$IDX awk ...`, a per-call env prefix that rebuilds the variable. `IDX` is now a plain shell variable set once at the top level (`IDX=$(index)`). This leaves two ways of getting the same value into awk: the prefix inside `render`, and the assignment outside it.

The stale-index hint interpolates $README but prints a bare `run 'bash scripts/adr-index.sh'`. When ADR_DIR is overridden, that command rewrites docs/adr/README.md instead of the file named in the message, so the hint is wrong.
